title: Call for individual mobility 2026-2027
content:
Artists and cultural professionals, who are:

  • legally residing in one of the Creative Europe countries, including the overseas countries and territories and outermost regions
  • 18 years of age or older
  • active in one of the following sectors: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts; No specific level of experience is required

    • The call for individual mobility allows applications from individuals and groups of up to 5 people.

    €85 per day of project implementation.

  • €400 for travel distances under 5.000 km
  • €800 travel distance from 5.000 km

    • The travel distance is calculated automatically in the application form, based on a one-way straight line. The European Commission distance calculator [link: /node/2919] may nevertheless be used for indicative estimates.

    The grant offers additional funding, if applicable:

  • green mobility top-up: €400
  • overseas countries and territories / Outermost regions top-up: €175
  • family top-up: €200 per child under 18 years old
  • visa top-up: €120
  • €30 per day of project implementation

title: Europe grows its network of experts in cultural heritage risk preparedness
content:
24 heritage professionals began their training in cultural heritage risk preparedness in June 2026 as part of a second group of specialists coming from 19 countries participating in the Creative Europe programme.

The training provided by the READY project involved two weeks of online learning followed by ten days of in-person training in Bucharest this September.

The new cohort joins the 24 professionals trained during the project's first year, forming a growing network dedicated to heritage risk management. In doing so, they have also built the knowledge and partnerships needed to protect heritage sites and associated living traditions from complex and cascading risks.

The training strengthens the ability of heritage professionals to safeguard immovable heritage and living traditions amid growing disaster risks, climate extremes and conflict. The participants developed practical skills and tools to assess and reduce disaster risk, improve emergency preparedness, coordinate cultural heritage first aid, and support early recovery.

title: Victoria will be the European Capital of Culture 2031 in Malta
content:
On 23 September 2026, the chairperson of the European Capitals of Culture expert panel announced Victoria as the recommended city for the European Capital of Culture 2031 title in Malta. The recommendation followed an assessment of the city’s application by the panel of independent experts.

After Valetta in 2018, Victoria will be the second Maltese city to hold this prestigious title.

After being the only city shortlisted, Victoria has been recommended by the panel of independent experts to become the 2031 European Capital of Culture in Malta.

In a world increasingly shaped by fragmentation and disconnection, Victoria seeks to turn its island condition into a source of connection. 
Through the theme “an Island of Islands”, Victoria 2031 explores the relationships between people, communities, places and Europe, seeing difference not as a source of isolation but as an opportunity for encounter, exchange and mutual enrichment. Slowness, care and courage provide the values for imagining more connected and collaborative futures.

title: Commission champions the next generation of European Capitals of Culture
content:
On 10 September 2026, the European Commission adopted its proposal for the new legal framework of the European Capitals of Culture action from 2034 to 2047. It will be discussed with both the European Parliament and the Council.

The European Capitals of Culture ’s current legal framework will come to an end in 2033. EU institutions thus need to determine how the action will be set up as of 2034 and ensure the initiative remains relevant, inclusive and impactful until 2047.

Based on thorough consultation and evaluation, the European Commission submitted a proposal to ensure that:

  • the action remains accessible and in line with EU priorities and current global challenges
  • the action reinforces its EU dimension
  • the right tools are provided to follow and react to the cities’ progress in implementing their programme and to plan for their legacy
  • the action remains visible by enhancing communication tools and activities

    • The proposal wants to bring more people in, make the process simpler and ensure the longer-term legacy of European Capitals of Culture.

title: European Heritage Days 2026: protecting Europe’s heritage at risk
content:
The EU strives to preserve cultural heritage under all circumstances, as reflected in the EU preparedness union strategy. Across Europe, communities are finding diverse ways to respond to these pressures with the support of the European Union.

Throughout September and October, the European Heritage Days 2026 invites people across Europe, under the theme “heritage at risk: revive, resist, reimagine” to discover how communities are protecting, restoring and reimagining their heritage for the future.

The 2026 European Heritage Days highlight how communities and EU-supported initiatives are protecting and adapting cultural heritage in response to climate change, societal shifts and other forms of threats, including conflict.

Link to the European Heritage Days website.

As climate change increases pressure on cultural sites and landscapes through extreme weather, flooding, fires and other natural hazards, protecting heritage also means finding ways to adapt. These challenges highlight how closely Europe’s natural and cultural heritage are connected.

title: Creative Europe in 2027: one last year before the new budget cycle
content:
Safeguarding cultural diversity and strengthening the competitiveness of the cultural and creative sectors remain Creative Europe’s general objectives.

In line with the Joint Declaration “Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe”, the Culture Compass for Europe and the European Democracy Shield, the programme will contribute to the protection of democracy, the green and digital transitions and the strengthening of social and economic resilience.

2027 will be the last year of implementation of the current Creative Europe programme. Its 402 million budget allocated for the year will ensure continuity in its actions, while addressing emerging challenges and paving the way towards its successor, AgoraEU.

Creative Europe will keep on contributing to the EU’s overarching priorities to support:

  • the greening efforts
  • the digital transition of the cultural and creative sectors
  • inclusion and gender equality practices
  • the role of culture in the EU international relations
